svg.title: Allocate $40,000 Without Spending the Refund Buffer
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-startup-capital-allocation; chart type: stacked_comparison; title: Allocate $40,000 Without Spending the Refund Buffer; subtitle: Four buckets fit the canonical $10,000–$50,000 startup envelope.; chapter number: 4; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Numeric values are dollar allocations for one $40,000 launch stack, totaling exactly $40,000. The 40%, 20%, 15%, and 25% allocation also maps to $10,000 and $50,000 examples. Acquisition cash and refundable deposits are not automatically expenses; a cash reserve is not a second profit deduction.; caption: A $10,000 launch should emphasize small, transferable positions. Do not interpret the capital range as sufficient to warehouse an entire premium suite or speculative tentpole allotment.; stages: label: Liquid resale inventory; value: $16,000; 40% of startup capital; numeric value: 16000.0; detail: Allocate $4,000 at a $10,000 launch or $20,000 at $50,000. Buy small positions with documented transferability and multiple demand outlets; cap correlated exposure to one team, venue, or event date.; label: Suite and hospitality deposits; value: $8,000; 20% of startup capital; numeric value: 8000.0; detail: Allocate $2,000 at a $10,000 launch or $10,000 at $50,000. Fund only contract-sized deposits with understood balance dates and cancellation terms. Customer prepayment cannot justify an uncovered refundable obligation.; label: Operating setup and runway; value: $6,000; 15% of startup capital; numeric value: 6000.0; detail: Allocate $1,500 at a $10,000 launch or $7,500 at $50,000. Budget applicable licensing, POS onboarding, bookkeeping, payment setup, and initial contractor coverage. Recurring spending must fit the $1,800–$11,000 monthly operating range.; label: Settlement and refund liquidity; value: $10,000; 25% of startup capital; numeric value: 10000.0; detail: Allocate $2,500 at a $10,000 launch or $12,500 at $50,000. Hold liquid cash for delayed exchange payout, replacement tickets, and customer refunds ahead of supplier recoveries. Increase the buffer when correlated event exposure rises.

text.title: Allocate $40,000 Without Spending the Refund Buffer
text.tspan: Allocate $40,000 Without Spending the Refund Buffer

rect.title: label: Liquid resale inventory; numeric value: 16000.0; value: $16,000; 40% of startup capital; detail: Allocate $4,000 at a $10,000 launch or $20,000 at $50,000. Buy small positions with documented transferability and multiple demand outlets; cap correlated exposure to one team, venue, or event date.

text.title: Liquid resale inventory: $16,000; 40% of startup capital
text.tspan: Liquid resale inventory: $16,000; 40% of startup capital

rect.title: label: Suite and hospitality deposits; numeric value: 8000.0; value: $8,000; 20% of startup capital; detail: Allocate $2,000 at a $10,000 launch or $10,000 at $50,000. Fund only contract-sized deposits with understood balance dates and cancellation terms. Customer prepayment cannot justify an uncovered refundable obligation.

text.title: Suite and hospitality deposits: $8,000; 20% of startup capital
text.tspan: Suite and hospitality deposits: $8,000; 20% of startup capital

rect.title: label: Operating setup and runway; numeric value: 6000.0; value: $6,000; 15% of startup capital; detail: Allocate $1,500 at a $10,000 launch or $7,500 at $50,000. Budget applicable licensing, POS onboarding, bookkeeping, payment setup, and initial contractor coverage. Recurring spending must fit the $1,800–$11,000 monthly operating range.

rect.title: label: Settlement and refund liquidity; numeric value: 10000.0; value: $10,000; 25% of startup capital; detail: Allocate $2,500 at a $10,000 launch or $12,500 at $50,000. Hold liquid cash for delayed exchange payout, replacement tickets, and customer refunds ahead of supplier recoveries. Increase the buffer when correlated event exposure rises.
